title: The Minimal Polynomial of cos 2π/n Is an Irreducible Factor of Tₙ − 1
description: The parent entry (OQ-02) proves the Chebyshev witness Tₙ(cos 2π/n) = 1, so cos 2π/n is a root of Tₙ − 1, and asks to identify the degree-φ(n)/2 irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1 that is its minimal polynomial. The exact degree φ(n)/2 is blocked on the absence of the maximal-real-subfield degree in Mathlib, but the structural half is not. This entry proves, with 0 axioms for all n ≥ 1, that minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) divides Tₙ − 1 in ℚ[X] and is irreducible — i.e. it really is an irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1 — together with cos 2π/n being integral over ℚ and the unconditional degree bound deg(minpoly) ≤ deg(Tₙ − 1).

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent: proves cos 2π/n is a root of Tₙ − 1 and asks to identify the degree-φ(n)/2 irreducible factor that is its minimal polynomial. This entry proves that factor is exactly minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) up to the still-open exact degree.

overview.historicalContext:
cos(2π/n) is the real part of a primitive n-th root of unity and generates the maximal real subfield ℚ(cos 2π/n) = ℚ(ζ_n)⁺ of the cyclotomic field, of degree φ(n)/2 over ℚ for n ≥ 3. Its minimal polynomial is therefore an irreducible polynomial of degree φ(n)/2 — and, because cos(2π/n) is a root of the Chebyshev polynomial equation Tₙ(x) = 1, it must be an irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1. The parent gallery entry (OQ-02) established the root fact Tₙ(cos 2π/n) = 1 over ℝ and isolated the exact degree formula as blocked on the missing maximal-real-subfield degree in Mathlib.

This entry closes the structural gap left by the parent: it proves in Lean, uniformly in n ≥ 1 and with 0 axioms, that the minimal polynomial of cos(2π/n) over ℚ genuinely divides Tₙ − 1 and is irreducible — the precise sense in which it is 'an irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1'. Only the exact value φ(n)/2 of its degree remains open, and that is a field-degree statement, not a statement about Chebyshev polynomials.
overview.problemStatement: Prove, with 0 axioms in Mathlib, that the minimal polynomial of cos(2π/n) over ℚ is an irreducible factor of the Chebyshev polynomial Tₙ − 1: (1) cos 2π/n is integral over ℚ; (2) minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) ∣ (Tₙ − 1); (3) minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) is irreducible; and (4) a degree bound deg(minpoly) ≤ deg(Tₙ − 1). The sharp degree φ(n)/2 is left as the remaining open refinement.
overview.proofStrategy: Everything hinges on lifting the parent's real identity to ℚ. (1) aeval (cos 2π/n) (Tₙ : ℚ[X]) = 1: rewrite aeval as eval of the base-changed polynomial (aeval_def, eval₂_eq_eval_map) and apply Polynomial.Chebyshev.map_T so Tₙ over ℚ maps to Tₙ over ℝ, then invoke the parent's cos_two_pi_div_chebyshev_root. (2) Tₙ − 1 ≠ 0: if it vanished, mapping to ℝ[X] forces Tₙ = 1 as a polynomial, contradicting (Tₙ).eval(cos(π/n)) = cos(n·π/n) = cos π = −1 (via T_real_cos and Real.cos_pi). (3) cos 2π/n is algebraic (root of the nonzero Tₙ − 1), hence integral over the field ℚ (IsAlgebraic.isIntegral). (4) minpoly.dvd applied to aeval(...) = 0 gives divisibility; minpoly.irreducible gives irreducibility; natDegree_le_of_dvd gives the degree bound.
keyInsights: The parent's root fact Tₙ(cos 2π/n) = 1 becomes a divisibility once phrased over ℚ: minpoly.dvd turns 'cos 2π/n is a root of Tₙ − 1' directly into 'minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) ∣ (Tₙ − 1)'.
Base change is the only real work: Polynomial.Chebyshev.map_T lets the real-valued parent identity be reused verbatim as a statement about the rational Chebyshev polynomial, where minpoly lives.

Nonzeroness of Tₙ − 1 (needed for integrality and the degree bound) is certified by a single off-root evaluation: cos(π/n), where Tₙ = cos π = −1 ≠ 1 for every n ≥ 1 — no Chebyshev degree lemma (absent from Mathlib) is required.
Irreducibility of the minimal polynomial is automatic once integrality is known, so 'irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1' is the combination of two clean Mathlib facts (minpoly.dvd and minpoly.irreducible).
The only thing still missing is the exact degree φ(n)/2, which is a field-degree fact about the maximal real subfield — not accessible from the Chebyshev picture alone and not yet in Mathlib.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 101 lines and 6 theorems proving that the minimal polynomial of cos 2π/n over ℚ is an irreducible factor of the Chebyshev polynomial Tₙ − 1: cos 2π/n is integral over ℚ, minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) ∣ (Tₙ − 1), the minimal polynomial is irreducible, and deg(minpoly) ≤ deg(Tₙ − 1).
conclusion.implications: This upgrades the parent's root fact (cos 2π/n is a root of Tₙ − 1) into the full structural statement of its OQ-02 open question — that the minimal polynomial is an irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1 — closing everything except the exact degree. The proof is a clean base-change reuse of the parent, showing that no new analysis is needed: minpoly.dvd and minpoly.irreducible do the work once the identity is phrased over ℚ. The only remaining gap is the field-degree value φ(n)/2, which needs the maximal-real-subfield degree still absent from Mathlib.
openQuestions: Prove deg(minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n)) = φ(n)/2 by formalizing [ℚ(ζ_n):ℚ(cos 2π/n)] = 2 (complex conjugation fixing the real subfield) against the cyclotomic degree [ℚ(ζ_n):ℚ] = φ(n).
Relate the irreducible factor minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) of Tₙ − 1 explicitly to the minimal polynomial of 2cos(2π/n) and to Φₙ via the substitution 2cos θ = ζ + ζ⁻¹.

crossReferences.description: Parent: proves cos 2π/n is a root of Tₙ − 1 (Chebyshev witness) and asks to identify the degree-φ(n)/2 irreducible factor that is its minimal polynomial. This entry proves that minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) is indeed an irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1, leaving only the exact degree open.
Grandparent: computes |Gal| = 3 for the cos(20°) minimal polynomial; the irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1 here is the general-n analogue of that concrete cubic.

The classical trisection impossibility hinges on deg minpoly(cos 20°) = 3 not being a power of 2. Since cos 20° = cos 2π/18, identifying minpoly ℚ (cos 2π/n) as the degree-φ(n)/2 irreducible factor of Tₙ − 1 (this entry) is precisely the general machinery that pins that degree — the constructibility obstruction behind the classical result.
